records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַזִּפִים֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּבְעָ֖תָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲל֨וֹא דָוִ֤ד מִסְתַּתֵּר֙ בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֔ה עַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃
records.gloss: And came the Ziphites to Saul [at] Gibeah, saying, [Is] not David hiding himself on [the] hill of the Hachilah, on [the] face of the Jeshimon?
pieces: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Did you know that David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the Jeshimon?"

L.1: And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is not David hiding himself on the hill of Hachilah, facing the Jeshimon?"

R.1: Some men from Ziph came to Saul at Gibeah. They told him, "David is hiding on Hachilah Hill, across from the desert wasteland."

decisions.choice: the Ziphites betray David a second time
decisions.reason: The people of Ziph had already told Saul where David was hiding, in almost the same words, and named the same hill of Hachilah (23:19). The story that follows runs closely parallel to chapter 24, where David also spared Saul's life.

decisions.choice: on the face of the Jeshimon: facing the wasteland
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "facing" or "overlooking", and it can also mean "east of", since the Hebrew way of giving directions faces east. The Jeshimon, "the desolate land", is the barren country that falls away toward the Dead Sea (23:19, 24).

decisions.choice: is not David hiding: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of announcing news: the Ziphites are telling Saul where David is.

decisions.choice: Did you know that
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the "is not ...?" question into a natural English question that brings news; Readable makes it a plain statement.

decisions.choice: the desert wasteland
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name Jeshimon; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

records.heading: David spares Saul a second time

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם שָׁא֗וּל וַיֵּ֨רֶד֙ אֶל־מִדְבַּר־זִ֔יף וְאִתּ֛וֹ שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־אֲלָפִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּחוּרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בְּמִדְבַּר־זִֽיף׃
records.gloss: And arose Saul and went down to [the] wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand men, chosen [ones] of Israel, to seek David in [the] wilderness of Ziph.
pieces: So Saul got up and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, taking three thousand of Israel's best soldiers, to hunt for David in the wilderness of Ziph.

L.2: And Saul rose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him [were] three thousand men, chosen [men] of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

R.2: So Saul took three thousand of the best soldiers in Israel and went down into the desert near Ziph to look for David.

decisions.choice: three thousand chosen men: picked fighting men
decisions.reason: "Chosen" men are men picked for their skill as soldiers. Saul took the same number when he hunted David near En Gedi (24:3).

decisions.choice: went down: from the hill country to the dry land
decisions.reason: Gibeah lies in the central hills; the wilderness of Ziph is lower ground in the southern hills of Judah, falling away to the east.

decisions.choice: best soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "chosen men" were; Literal keeps "chosen".

decisions.choice: the desert near Ziph
decisions.reason: Readable uses "desert" for the wild, dry land the Hebrew calls a wilderness.

records.source: וַיִּ֨חַן שָׁא֜וּל בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹ֖ן עַל־הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וְדָוִד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיַּ֕רְא כִּ֣י בָ֥א שָׁא֛וּל אַחֲרָ֖יו הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃
records.gloss: And camped Saul on [the] hill of the Hachilah, which [is] on [the] face of the Jeshimon, by the road; and David [was] staying in the wilderness, and he saw that had come Saul after him to the wilderness.
pieces: Saul made camp beside the road on the hill of Hachilah, facing the Jeshimon. David was living out in the wilderness, and he realized that Saul had followed him there.

L.3: And Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which [is] facing the Jeshimon, beside the road, while David was staying in the wilderness. And he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.

R.3: Saul set up camp beside the road on Hachilah Hill, across from the desert wasteland. David was staying out in the desert, and he found out that Saul had come after him.

decisions.choice: David was staying in the wilderness: not on the hill itself
decisions.reason: Saul camps on the very hill the Ziphites had named, but David has moved on, deeper into the wilderness, where he can watch the camp.

decisions.choice: he saw: he became aware
decisions.reason: "See" here means to learn or realize. David hears of Saul's coming and then sends spies to make sure (verse 4).

decisions.choice: realized; found out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "saw" here; Literal keeps "saw".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד מְרַגְּלִ֑ים וַיֵּ֕דַע כִּֽי־בָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־נָכֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And sent David spies, and knew that had come Saul for certain.
pieces: So David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had indeed arrived.

L.4: And David sent out spies, and he knew that Saul had certainly come.

R.4: So David sent out spies, and he learned that Saul really had come.

decisions.choice: for certain: beyond doubt
decisions.reason: The two words mean "for sure" or "with certainty", as in 23:23. They could also be read as a place, "to Nacon", or as "to a fixed place", but no such place is known here.

decisions.choice: scouts
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "scouts" for men sent to watch an enemy's movements; Literal and Readable say "spies".

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶֽל־הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָנָה־שָׁ֣ם שָׁאוּל֒ וַיַּ֣רְא דָּוִ֗ד אֶת־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁכַב־שָׁ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וְאַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־נֵ֖ר שַׂר־צְבָא֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וְהָעָ֖ם חֹנִ֥ים סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And arose David and came to the place where had camped there Saul, and saw David the place where lay there Saul and Abner son of Ner, commander of his army; and Saul [was] lying in the encampment, and the people [were] camping around him.
pieces: Then David set out and came to the place where Saul had made camp. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army, were lying. Saul lay inside the ring of the camp, with the troops camped all around him.

L.5: And David rose and came to the place where Saul had camped. And David saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army; and Saul was lying inside the encampment, and the people were camping around him.

R.5: Then David went to the place where Saul's army had set up camp. He could see where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the army commander, were lying down. Saul was lying in the middle of the camp, and his soldiers were camped all around him.

decisions.choice: Abner son of Ner, commander of his army
decisions.reason: Abner was Saul's cousin and the commander of his army (14:50-51). As the king's chief soldier he had the duty of guarding him, which David will throw back at him (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: the encampment: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: As in 17:20, the word names a circle or track, probably the inner ring of the camp, perhaps marked by carts or baggage. The king slept at the center, protected on every side.

decisions.choice: the people: the army
decisions.reason: "The people" here are Saul's fighting men camped in the field.

decisions.choice: the troops; his soldiers
decisions.reason: For the people as an army in the field, Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "soldiers"; Literal keeps "the people".

decisions.choice: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the circle; Readable says "the middle of the camp".

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן דָּוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אֶל־אֲחִימֶ֣לֶךְ הַחִתִּ֗י וְאֶל־אֲבִישַׁ֨י בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֜ה אֲחִ֤י יוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מִֽי־יֵרֵ֥ד אִתִּ֛י אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֔י אֲנִ֖י אֵרֵ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And said Abishai, I will go down with you.
pieces: David turned to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and asked, "Who will go down with me into the camp, to Saul?" "I will go with you," Abishai answered.

L.6: And David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, saying, "Who will go down with me to Saul, into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go down with you."

R.6: David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai, Joab's brother, whose mother was Zeruiah. He asked them, "Who will go down with me into Saul's camp?" Abishai said, "I will go with you."

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up
decisions.reason: "Answered" often means simply that someone began to speak in response to a situation, not to a question.

decisions.choice: Ahimelech the Hittite: a foreigner in David's band
decisions.reason: The Hittites were one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel (Genesis 23:3; Deuteronomy 7:1). Some served Israel's kings, as Uriah the Hittite later served David (2 Samuel 11:3). This Ahimelech is not the priest of chapters 21-22.

decisions.choice: Abishai son of Zeruiah: David's nephew
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel are usually named after her. Abishai was to become one of David's leading warriors (2 Samuel 23:18).

decisions.choice: whose mother was Zeruiah
decisions.reason: Readable says who Zeruiah was, so that the reader does not take her for Abishai's father.

records.source: וַיָּבֹא֩ דָוִ֨ד וַאֲבִישַׁ֥י׀אֶל־הָעָם֮ לַיְלָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שָׁא֗וּל שֹׁכֵ֤ב יָשֵׁן֙ בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וַחֲנִית֥וֹ מְעוּכָֽה־בָאָ֖רֶץ מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וְאַבְנֵ֣ר וְהָעָ֔ם שֹׁכְבִ֖ים סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And came David and Abishai to the people by night, and look, Saul [was] lying asleep in the encampment, and his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Abner and the people lying around him.
pieces: So David and Abishai went to the troops by night. There was Saul, lying asleep inside the ring of the camp, his spear thrust into the ground by his head, while Abner and the troops lay around him.

L.7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and look, Saul was lying asleep inside the encampment, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Abner and the people were lying around him.

R.7: That night David and Abishai went down to the army. They found Saul asleep in the middle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground near his head. Abner and the soldiers were lying all around him.

decisions.choice: look: the scene through David's eyes
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what David and Abishai find as they come into the camp.

decisions.choice: his spear stuck in the ground: the king's weapon
decisions.reason: Saul's spear marks his royal power and is never far from him (22:6). It is the spear he twice threw at David (18:10-11; 19:10). Stuck upright in the ground by his head, it also showed where the king slept.

decisions.choice: the troops; the army, the soldiers
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, for the people as an army in the field.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲבִישַׁי֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד סִגַּ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־אוֹיִבְךָ֖ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּה֩ אַכֶּ֨נּוּ נָ֜א בַּחֲנִ֤ית וּבָאָ֨רֶץ֙ פַּ֣עַם אַחַ֔ת וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁנֶ֖ה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Abishai to David, Has shut up God today your enemy into your hand; and now let me strike him, please, with the spear and into the ground [with] one stroke, and not will I do [it] twice to him.
pieces: Abishai said to David, "God has put your enemy in your power today. Now please let me drive the spear through him into the ground. One blow is all it will take; I will not need another."

L.8: And Abishai said to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hand today. And now, please let me strike him with the spear, into the ground, with one stroke, and I will not [strike] him a second time."

R.8: Abishai said to David, "Today God has let you catch your enemy. Let me pin him to the ground with the spear. I will only need to hit him once."

decisions.choice: delivered: shut up, handed over
decisions.reason: The verb means to close someone in so that they cannot escape, and so to hand them over (23:7, 20; 24:19).

decisions.choice: your enemy into your hand: as in the cave
decisions.reason: David's men said almost the same in the cave at En Gedi (24:5). Abishai reads the moment the same way: God has given Saul to David to kill.

decisions.choice: one stroke, and not twice: a single blow will do
decisions.reason: Abishai promises a quick, clean kill: one thrust of the spear will be enough.

decisions.choice: in your power; let you catch
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "into your hand"; Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־אֲבִישַׁ֖י אַל־תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֑הוּ כִּ֠י מִ֣י שָׁלַ֥ח יָד֛וֹ בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה וְנִקָּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And said David to Abishai, Do not destroy him, for who has stretched out his hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh and been guiltless?
pieces: But David said to Abishai, "Do not kill him. Who could raise his hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed and not be held guilty?"

L.9: And David said to Abishai, "Do not destroy him, for who has stretched out his hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed and been guiltless?"

R.9: But David told Abishai, "Do not kill him! No one can attack the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed and still be innocent."

decisions.choice: the anointed of Yahweh: the king Yahweh has set apart
decisions.reason: As at 24:7: Saul was set apart as king when Samuel poured oil on his head at Yahweh's command (10:1), so to kill him would be to strike at Yahweh, who chose him. David had already refused on these grounds in the cave (24:7, 11).

decisions.choice: stretch out his hand against: attack, harm
decisions.reason: To "send out the hand" against someone is to do them violence (22:17; 24:7, 11).

decisions.choice: been guiltless: gone unpunished
decisions.reason: The verb means to be clear of guilt and so free from punishment. The question expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: destroy: kill
decisions.reason: The verb, "bring to ruin", here means to take Saul's life.

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: As at 24:7, Readable spells out what "the LORD's anointed" means; Literal and Balanced keep the title.

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what Abishai means to do; Literal keeps "destroy".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִם־יְהוָ֖ה יִגָּפֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־יוֹמ֤וֹ יָבוֹא֙ וָמֵ֔ת א֧וֹ בַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה יֵרֵ֖ד וְנִסְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said David, [As] lives Yahweh, surely Yahweh will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or into battle he will go down and be swept away.
pieces: David went on, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who will strike him down. Either his time will come and he will die, or he will go out to battle and be cut down.

L.10: And David said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, surely {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike him; or his day will come and he will die; or he will go down into battle and be swept away.

R.10: David said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will strike Saul down. Or Saul will die when his time comes, or he will be killed in battle.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: an oath
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath (14:39; 20:3). David binds himself to leave Saul's death to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will strike him: judgment belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: David will not take Saul's life; if Saul is to die, Yahweh will see to it, as David told Saul in the cave (24:13, 16). Yahweh struck down Nabal in just this way (25:38).

decisions.choice: his day will come; be swept away
decisions.reason: "His day" is the day fixed for his death. The last verb means to be carried off or perish. Saul does in fact die in battle against the Philistines (31:1-6).

decisions.choice: be cut down; be killed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how a man is "swept away" in battle; Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵֽיהוָ֔ה מִשְּׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠עַתָּה קַח־נָ֨א אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֜ית אֲשֶׁ֧ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֛יו וְאֶת־צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם וְנֵ֥לֲכָה לָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Far be it to me from Yahweh from stretching out my hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh; and now take, please, the spear that [is] at his head and the jug of the water, and let us go for ourselves.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from ever raising my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed! Now pick up the spear beside his head and the water jug, and let us be on our way."

L.11: Far be it from me, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to stretch out my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. But now, please take the spear that [is] at his head and the jug of water, and let us go."

R.11: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from ever attacking the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed! Now grab the spear and the water jug near his head, and let us leave."

decisions.choice: far be it from me from Yahweh: Yahweh forbid that I should
decisions.reason: A strong refusal, made in Yahweh's sight, with the same words David used in the cave (24:7).

decisions.choice: the jug of water: a traveler's water flask
decisions.reason: In the dry wilderness a man kept water close at hand through the night. The spear and the water jug from beside the king's head would prove that David had stood over him while he slept (verse 16), as the corner of his robe had done in the cave (24:5, 12).

decisions.choice: May the LORD keep me from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the oath-like refusal into a wish addressed to the LORD; Literal keeps "far be it from me".

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֜ית וְאֶת־צַפַּ֤חַת הַמַּ֨יִם֙ מֵרַאֲשֹׁתֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין רֹאֶה֩ וְאֵ֨ין יוֹדֵ֜עַ וְאֵ֣ין מֵקִ֗יץ כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ יְשֵׁנִ֔ים כִּ֚י תַּרְדֵּמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה נָפְלָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And took David the spear and the jug of the water from at [the] head of Saul, and they went for themselves; and [there was] none seeing and none knowing and none waking, for all of them [were] sleeping, for a deep sleep of Yahweh had fallen upon them.
pieces: So David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and the two of them left. No one saw them, no one knew, and no one woke up. They were all asleep, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sent a deep sleep on them.

L.12: So David took the spear and the jug of water from beside Saul's head, and they went away. And no one saw, and no one knew, and no one woke up, for all of them [were] asleep, because a deep sleep from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had fallen on them.

R.12: So David took the spear and the water jug that were near Saul's head, and he and Abishai left. Nobody saw them. Nobody knew what had happened. Nobody woke up. They were all sound asleep, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made them sleep very deeply.

decisions.choice: a deep sleep of Yahweh: a sleep sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word names an unusually heavy sleep, one that Yahweh brings (Genesis 2:21; 15:12). The camp's failure to wake is Yahweh's doing, not only the guards' carelessness.

decisions.choice: David took: David himself takes them
decisions.reason: David had told Abishai to take the spear and jug (verse 11), but the narrator says that David took them. Either David carried them himself or the act is credited to him as leader; what matters is that they came from beside the king's head.

decisions.choice: none seeing, none knowing, none waking
decisions.reason: Three short clauses in a row stress how completely the camp slept.

decisions.choice: he and Abishai
decisions.reason: Readable names the two who left.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר דָּוִד֙ הָעֵ֔בֶר וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־רֹאשׁ־הָהָ֖ר מֵֽרָחֹ֑ק רַ֥ב הַמָּק֖וֹם בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And crossed over David [to] the other side and stood on [the] top of the mountain from far; great [was] the space between them.
pieces: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill some way off, with a wide space between them.

L.13: And David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain far off; great [was] the space between them.

R.13: Then David crossed over to the other side of the valley. He stood on top of a hill a long way from the camp.

decisions.choice: far off, with a great space between them
decisions.reason: David stands where his voice will carry across the valley but where no soldier can reach him quickly. In the cave he had spoken to Saul from close behind him (24:9).

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hilltop
decisions.reason: The word covers anything from a mountain to a hill or the hill country. Here it is a height across a valley from Saul's camp.

decisions.choice: hill
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "hill" for the height in this hill country; Literal keeps "mountain".

decisions.choice: of the valley
decisions.reason: Readable says what lay between David and the camp.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א דָוִ֜ד אֶל־הָעָ֗ם וְאֶל־אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־נֵר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא תַעֲנֶ֖ה אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיַּ֤עַן אַבְנֵר֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה קָרָ֥אתָ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
records.gloss: And called David to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, Will you not answer, Abner? And answered Abner and said, Who [are] you [that] you have called to the king?
pieces: David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, "Abner, are you not going to answer?" Abner replied, "Who are you, to call out to the king?"

L.14: And David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" And Abner answered and said, "Who [are] you [that] you have called to the king?"

R.14: David shouted to the soldiers and to Abner son of Ner, "Abner! Answer me!" Abner called back, "Who are you? Why are you shouting at the king?"

decisions.choice: will you not answer: a summons
decisions.reason: The question is a call to wake up and respond.

decisions.choice: who are you that you have called to the king: a rebuke
decisions.reason: Abner asks who the caller is and also scolds him for shouting at the king's camp in the night. He does not yet know the voice.

decisions.choice: the troops; the soldiers
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, for the people as an army in the field.

decisions.choice: Who are you? Why are you shouting at the king?
decisions.reason: Readable splits Abner's question in two to bring out the rebuke in it.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־אַבְנֵ֜ר הֲלוֹא־אִ֣ישׁ אַתָּ֗ה וּמִ֤י כָמ֨וֹךָ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלָ֨מָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֶל־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּי־בָא֙ אַחַ֣ד הָעָ֔ם לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said David to Abner, [Are] not you a man? And who [is] like you in Israel? And why have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For came one of the people to destroy the king your lord.
pieces: David said to Abner, "You are a man, are you not? Who else in Israel is like you? Then why did you not guard your lord the king? One of the people came in to kill the king, your lord.

L.15: And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who [is] like you in Israel? Then why have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king your lord.

R.15: David said to Abner, "You are a brave man, are you not? There is no one in Israel like you! So why did you not guard your master, the king? Someone came into the camp to kill your master, the king!

decisions.choice: are you not a man? who is like you? mockery
decisions.reason: David praises Abner as Israel's greatest soldier in order to shame him: the man with no equal has let his king lie unguarded.

decisions.choice: one of the people: someone
decisions.reason: "One of the people" means an ordinary man. David means himself or Abishai, though he does not yet say so.

decisions.choice: kept watch: guarded
decisions.reason: Abner's duty as commander was to watch over the king's person. David repeats the charge in verse 16.

decisions.choice: a brave man
decisions.reason: Readable adds "brave" to show that David is speaking of Abner's standing as a fighter.

decisions.choice: your master
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for the lord a commander serves.

records.source: לֹא־ט֞וֹב הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂיתָ֒ חַי־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י בְנֵי־מָ֨וֶת֙ אַתֶּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־שְׁמַרְתֶּ֛ם עַל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֣ה׀רְאֵ֗ה אֵֽי־חֲנִ֥ית הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְאֶת־צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Not good [is] the thing this that you have done. [As] lives Yahweh, surely sons of death [are] you, who have not kept watch over your lord, over [the] anointed of Yahweh. And now see where [is] the spear of the king and the jug of the water that [was] at his head.
pieces: You have not done well at all. As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you all deserve to die, because you did not guard your lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. Now look around. Where is the king's spear, and the water jug that was by his head?"

L.16: This thing that you have done [is] not good. [As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you [are] sons of death, because you have not kept watch over your lord, over {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. And now see where the king's spear [is], and the jug of water that [was] at his head."

R.16: You have not done your job well! As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you and your men deserve to die. You did not protect your master, the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed. Look around! Where is the king's spear? Where is the water jug that was near his head?"

decisions.choice: sons of death: men who deserve to die
decisions.reason: "Son of death" means someone who has earned death (20:31; 2 Samuel 12:5). The word "you" is plural: Abner and the men who should have kept watch.

decisions.choice: over your lord, over the anointed of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The second phrase restates the first. The man they failed to guard was not only their master but Yahweh's anointed king.

decisions.choice: the spear and the water jug: the proof
decisions.reason: The missing objects show that someone stood by the sleeping king, as the cut corner of the robe did in 24:12.

decisions.choice: you and your men
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "you" here is plural.

decisions.choice: your master, the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: As in verses 9 and 15.

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֤ר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דָּוִ֔ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲקוֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד קוֹלִ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And recognized Saul [the] voice of David and said, [Is] this your voice, my son David? And said David, My voice, my lord the king.
pieces: Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David replied, "It is, my lord the king."

L.17: And Saul recognized David's voice and said, "[Is] this your voice, my son David?" And David said, "[It is] my voice, my lord the king."

R.17: Saul knew it was David's voice. He called out, "Is that you, David my son?" David answered, "Yes, it is, my lord the king."

decisions.choice: is this your voice, my son David?
decisions.reason: Saul asks the same question as at En Gedi (24:17). Calling David "my son" is tender, and David was in fact his son-in-law (18:27).

decisions.choice: my lord the king: a subject's address
decisions.reason: David speaks to Saul with full respect as his king, even while Saul hunts him.

decisions.choice: Is that you
decisions.reason: Readable says what Saul means by "your voice"; Literal and Balanced keep the wording.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥י רֹדֵ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּמַה־בְּיָדִ֖י רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said, Why this [is] my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done, and what [is] in my hand [of] evil?
pieces: He went on, "Why is my lord chasing after his servant? What have I done? What wrong have I committed?

L.18: And he said, "Why [is] this my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done, and what evil [is] in my hand?

R.18: Then he said, "My lord, why are you chasing me, your servant? What have I done? What crime have I committed?

decisions.choice: his servant: David speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" or "his servant" was a polite way to address someone of higher rank (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7-8). David puts himself below Saul as his subject.

decisions.choice: what evil is in my hand: what wrong have I done
decisions.reason: The hand stands for what a person does. David had made the same claim in the cave (24:12) and to Jonathan (20:1).

decisions.choice: pursuing: hunting down
decisions.reason: The verb is used of chasing an enemy. David repeats the picture of the hunt in verse 20.

decisions.choice: My lord, why are you chasing me, your servant?
decisions.reason: Readable turns David's third-person way of speaking into direct address, keeping "your servant".

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה יִֽשְׁמַֽע־נָא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ אִם־יְהוָ֞ה הֱסִֽיתְךָ֥ בִי֙ יָרַ֣ח מִנְחָ֔ה וְאִ֣ם׀בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֗ם אֲרוּרִ֥ים הֵם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־גֵרְשׁ֣וּנִי הַיּ֗וֹם מֵהִסְתַּפֵּ֜חַ בְּנַחֲלַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֥ךְ עֲבֹ֖ד אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now let hear, please, my lord the king [the] words of his servant: If Yahweh has stirred you up against me, let him smell an offering; but if [the] sons of man, cursed [are] they before Yahweh, for they have driven me out today from attaching myself to [the] inheritance of Yahweh, saying, Go, serve other gods.
pieces: Now please, my lord the king, listen to the words of your servant. If it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who has stirred you up against me, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept an offering. But if it is human beings, may they be cursed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! For they have driven me out today from my share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s inheritance, as if to say, 'Go, serve other gods.'

L.19: And now, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has stirred you up against me, let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} smell an offering; but if [it is] the sons of man, cursed [are] they before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for they have driven me out today from having a share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s inheritance, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'

R.19: My lord the king, please listen to what your servant has to say. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has turned you against me, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept an offering and be pleased. But if people have turned you against me, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} curse them! Today they have chased me out of the land that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is as if they were telling me, 'Go away and worship other gods.'

decisions.choice: let him smell an offering: may Yahweh accept a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Yahweh is said to "smell" the soothing smell of a sacrifice when he accepts it and his anger is turned away (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 26:31). If Yahweh is behind Saul's hatred, David asks that an offering be made to set things right with him.

decisions.choice: the sons of man: human beings
decisions.reason: The phrase sets people against Yahweh: if Saul's anger comes from slanderers and not from Yahweh, they are the guilty ones (24:10).

decisions.choice: driven me out from attaching myself to the inheritance of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to join oneself to or have a part in something. "The inheritance of Yahweh" is the land and people of Israel, which belong to Yahweh as his own possession (Deuteronomy 32:9; 2 Samuel 14:16; 20:19). Hunted out of Israel, David loses his place among Yahweh's people.

decisions.choice: go, serve other gods: exile from Yahweh's land
decisions.reason: In the ancient world each land was thought to belong to its own god, and Yahweh's worship was bound to his land, his people and his sanctuary (Deuteronomy 4:27-28; 28:36, 64; 2 Kings 5:17; Ruth 1:15-16). To drive David out of Israel was, in effect, to send him where other gods were worshiped and cut him off from the worship of Yahweh. David does not say that he will serve other gods; he says that his enemies are as good as telling him to. He goes to the Philistines in the next chapter (27:1).

decisions.choice: saying: as if to say
decisions.reason: No one has actually spoken the words. "Saying" gives the meaning of what David's enemies are doing to him.

decisions.choice: as if to say; It is as if they were telling me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "saying" gives the effect of their actions, not words anyone spoke.

decisions.choice: the land that belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what Yahweh's inheritance is here; Literal and Balanced keep "inheritance".

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־יִפֹּ֤ל דָּֽמִי֙ אַ֔רְצָה מִנֶּ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָצָ֞א מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֣שׁ אֶחָ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִרְדֹּ֥ף הַקֹּרֵ֖א בֶּהָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now let not fall my blood to the ground away from [the] presence of Yahweh, for has come out [the] king of Israel to seek a flea, one, as hunts the partridge in the mountains.
pieces: So now, do not let my blood be spilled on the ground far from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The king of Israel has come out to hunt for a single flea, the way someone chases a partridge through the hills."

L.20: And now, do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as one hunts the partridge in the mountains."

R.20: Do not let me be killed far away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence. The king of Israel has come out to look for one tiny flea! He is hunting me like someone hunting a partridge in the hills."

decisions.choice: let not my blood fall to the ground: do not let me be killed
decisions.reason: Blood falling to the ground is a picture of violent death (2 Samuel 14:11; 1 Kings 1:52).

decisions.choice: away from the presence of Yahweh: in a foreign land
decisions.reason: David picks up verse 19: if he is driven from Israel, he will die far from the land where Yahweh is worshiped.

decisions.choice: a single flea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "a single flea", the same picture David used in 24:15 of how little he matters. An ancient Greek translation reads "to seek my life" here. The Hebrew reading fits the hunting picture that follows.

decisions.choice: the partridge: a hunted bird of the hills
decisions.reason: The bird is named "the caller", probably a partridge, which runs along the ground and is chased until it tires. The name echoes David "calling" from the hilltop (verse 14). The bird cannot be identified for certain.

decisions.choice: be killed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "my blood fall to the ground"; Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁא֨וּל חָטָ֜אתִי שׁ֣וּב בְּנִֽי־דָוִ֗ד כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אָרַ֤ע לְךָ֙ ע֔וֹד תַּ֠חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקְרָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֛י בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הִנֵּ֥ה הִסְכַּ֛לְתִּי וָאֶשְׁגֶּ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And said Saul, I have sinned. Return, my son David, for not will I harm you again, because was precious my life in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have erred very greatly.
pieces: Then Saul said, "I have sinned. My son David, come back. Since you held my life precious today, I will not do you harm again. I have been a fool, and I have done a very great wrong."

L.21: And Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will not harm you again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have gone very greatly astray."

R.21: Saul said, "I have done wrong. Come back, David my son. You thought my life was worth saving today, so I will never try to hurt you again. I have been very foolish. I have made a terrible mistake."

decisions.choice: I have sinned: Saul's confession
decisions.reason: Saul admits his wrong, as he did to Samuel (15:24, 30) and wept over it at En Gedi (24:17-18). Yet David does not come back to him, and soon flees to the Philistines (27:1).

decisions.choice: my life was precious in your eyes: you valued my life
decisions.reason: David held Saul's life too dear to take it. David answers with the same picture in verse 24.

decisions.choice: acted foolishly and erred very greatly
decisions.reason: "Act foolishly" is the verb Samuel used of Saul in 13:13. The second verb means to go astray or blunder, and the words that follow make it very great.

decisions.choice: I have done wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says "done wrong" for the confession; Literal and Balanced keep "sinned".

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַן דָּוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה חֲנִ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְיַעֲבֹ֛ר אֶחָ֥ד מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֖ים וְיִקָּחֶֽהָ׃
records.gloss: And answered David and said, Look, the spear of the king! And let cross over one of the young men and take it.
pieces: David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Let one of your young men come across and get it.

L.22: And David answered and said, "Look, the king's spear! Let one of the young men come over and take it.

R.22: David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Send one of your young men over to get it.

decisions.choice: the king's spear
alternatives: Here is the spear, O king!
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text could be read "Here is the spear, O king!", while the reading noted in the margin is "Here is the king's spear". The text follows the margin. The meaning is the same: David hands back the king's spear.

decisions.choice: the young men: Saul's soldiers
decisions.reason: "Young men" here are fighting men or attendants of the king (14:1; 21:3).

decisions.choice: your young men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "your" to show that the young men are Saul's.

records.source: וַֽיהוָה֙ יָשִׁ֣יב לָאִ֔ישׁ אֶת־צִדְקָת֖וֹ וְאֶת־אֱמֻנָת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר֩ נְתָנְךָ֨יְהוָ֤ה׀הַיּוֹם֙ בְּיָ֔ד וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֔יתִי לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh will repay to each his righteousness and his faithfulness, for gave you Yahweh today into [my] hand, and not was I willing to stretch out my hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} repays each person for his righteousness and his faithfulness. Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you in my power, but I would not raise my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.

L.23: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will repay each man [for] his righteousness and his faithfulness; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you into [my] hand today, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} rewards each person who is righteous and faithful. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} put you in my power today, but I would not attack the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will repay each: Yahweh rewards right conduct
decisions.reason: David trusts Yahweh to reward the one who has acted rightly and loyally, as he said in 24:13, 16. Righteousness here is doing what is right toward another, and faithfulness is keeping faith with one's king.

decisions.choice: into hand: into my hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has simply "into a hand", the hand being David's.

decisions.choice: not willing: I refused
decisions.reason: The verb means to be willing or to consent. David chose not to strike, though he could have.

decisions.choice: in my power
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, Balanced and Readable give the sense of "into hand".

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְלָ֧ה נַפְשְׁךָ֛ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בְּעֵינָ֑י כֵּ֣ן תִּגְדַּ֤ל נַפְשִׁי֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיַצִּלֵ֖נִי מִכָּל־צָרָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And look, as was great your life this day in my eyes, so may be great my life in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and may he deliver me from all distress.
pieces: Just as your life mattered greatly to me today, so may my life matter greatly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescue me from every trouble."

L.24: And look, as your life was great in my eyes this day, so may my life be great in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deliver me from all distress."

R.24: Today I treated your life as precious. In the same way, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} treat my life as precious and save me from all my troubles."

decisions.choice: as your life was great in my eyes: an answer to Saul
decisions.reason: David takes up Saul's words in verse 21 ("my life was precious in your eyes"), with a word meaning "great" or "highly valued". He asks Yahweh, not Saul, to value his life in return.

decisions.choice: may my life be great; may he deliver me: a prayer
decisions.reason: The verbs express a wish addressed to Yahweh. David puts his safety in Yahweh's hands rather than in Saul's promise.

decisions.choice: treat my life as precious
decisions.reason: Readable uses the same words for both halves to show that David is answering Saul.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד בָּר֤וּךְ אַתָּה֙ בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֔ד גַּ֚ם עָשֹׂ֣ה תַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְגַ֖ם יָכֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ לְדַרְכּ֔וֹ וְשָׁא֖וּל שָׁ֥ב לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And said Saul to David, Blessed [are] you, my son David; both doing you will do, and also prevailing you will prevail. And went David on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
pieces: Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David! Whatever you set out to do, you will accomplish it, and you will win in the end." Then David went his way, and Saul returned home.

L.25: And Saul said to David, "Blessed [are] you, my son David! You will surely do [great things], and you will surely prevail." And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

R.25: Saul said to David, "You are blessed, David my son! You will do great things, and you will win in the end." Then David went on his way, and Saul went back home.

decisions.choice: doing you will do, prevailing you will prevail: certainty
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled to make it certain: David will surely accomplish what he undertakes and surely overcome. Saul had said as much at En Gedi, that David would be king (24:21).

decisions.choice: David went his way; Saul returned to his place
decisions.reason: The two men part. This is the last time they meet in the story: David goes to the Philistines (27:1), and Saul dies on Mount Gilboa (31:1-6). "His place" is Saul's home at Gibeah.

decisions.choice: do great things; win in the end
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "great things" as the implied object of "do"; Balanced and Readable say what the doubled verbs promise.

decisions.choice: home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "home" for "his place".
